name: Languid Lavender
lede: Languid Lavender is a very pale purple named for the lavender plant, one of several near-duplicate names the ISCC-NBS system lists for roughly the same pale purple.

sections.title: One of many pale purples
sections.body: The library records Languid Lavender from the ISCC-NBS system's 1955 block 213 [1]. The name pairs [[lavender]] with "languid"; the ISCC-NBS lists for this stretch of pale purple are unusually crowded with commercial names, which our library does not treat as separate colors here [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 83, chroma 11, hue 314 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "very pale purple" block, Munsell 5.6P 8.2/3.2, and [[violet]] than to plain grey [1]. The nearest named color in the library is [[thistle|Thistle]], about 5.2 units away by CIEDE2000 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 32 of 23,781 paintings, 0.13 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 22 [2]. That makes it rarer than 60 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 5 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.3 percent of that century's paintings, 2.1 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light, in 59 percent of its appearances [2].

The earliest match is dated 1515, by Andrea del Sarto; that is 440 years before the name's own first record, in 1955, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
